newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon approves budget spending increase.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon approves budget spending increase.

text.p: The Lebanese government approved on Saturday a 233 billion Lebanese pounds increase in proposed 1997 budget spending but decided to offset much of it by cutting subsidies to electricity consumers by 200 billion pounds.

The net increase of 33 billion pounds ($21 million) raised spending by 0.5 percent and widened the deficit of planned income against expenditure to about 37.5 percent, Information Minister Bassem al-Sabaa told reporters.
He gave no further details, but the original budget draft approved by the government last September proposed expenditures of 6,400 billion pounds against income of 4,100 billion.

Most of the 233 billion pounds additional spending approved on Saturday was proposed last week by the parliamentary finance committee, but the government added further sums for agriculture and public works on Saturday, a committee member said.
The size of the proposed deficit is expected to be a major issue when parliament holds its three-day budget debate starting on Wednesday.

Some economists point out the government has routinely and greatly overrun deficit targets in the past few years and say it should stop presenting parliament with budgets that they say are fictitious.
They point out that the 1996 deficit, planned at 2,428 billion pounds or 38 percent of expenditure, ended up at 3,692 billion pounds or 51 percent.

The economists say the high interest rates that the government is maintaining on treasury bills in order to attract funds to finance mushrooming public debt that the deficit is causing are sucking in liquidity and stifling private sector economic activity.
